Maintain the same frontage alignment for the secondary notch so the public opening remains coherent.
Bring the cantilever onset downward to expose more of the ground threshold and improve the public edge response.

Keep the secondary notch consistent with the frontage-facing public threshold to strengthen a single readable access figure.

rationale: The mass is generally coherent across views: a single dominant bent bar with a stepped/capped upper form reads consistently and does not visibly self-collide. However, for the neighborhood_living brief it is too sealed at the ground and the public-void logic is weak; the blue access edge is not answered by a clearly legible entry court, seam, or undercut, so the semantic street threshold requirement is only partially satisfied. The silhouette is not merely generic box extrusion, but the section remains more like a compact stacked object than a building with an active neighborhood ground condition. Reference language supports courtyard/terrace/bridge principles, yet the candidate has not translated those into a sufficiently public void or access-facing gesture. Program fit therefore fails the hard pass even though the mass is repairable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion/cultural than compact active-bar living; do not copy the rounded roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise massing with a carved central void and a bridge-like upper connector can create a legible public threshold for neighborhood program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Campus-like multi-building composition is broader than this candidate; transfer the courtyard hierarchy, not the podium-tower scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced low-rise blocks organized around a courtyard can support mixed neighborhood use while preserving a clear open-space figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the strong porous perimeter and roof articulation shown here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An elongated mass with a central atrium and folded roof suggests a coherent public interior/exterior sequence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More articulated and distributed than the candidate; use this for section logic, not as a literal profile.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Layered terrace-like sections and connected wings can express neighborhood scale while maintaining a readable central void.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is much more monolithic; transfer the void-and-bridge relationship instead of the multi-wing plan.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking wings with voids under elevated blocks can produce an active ground threshold and clear hierarchy.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied in the supplied views.
Access edge response is not clearly aligned to the verified frontage; the ground condition reads more sealed than public.
Do not overvalue the stepped cap: it is coherent, but not yet a program-meaningful terrace or inhabited section.
